And algorithms decide which news gets prioritized in our social media feeds and search results, shaping what hundreds of millions of people are exposed to. fragments.text: Journalism has traditionally been the backbone of democracy, guiding public understanding of complex issues through investigation and ethical reporting. But the rise of AI in journalism paired with platform driven news distribution is fragmenting this shared reality. Digital platforms now curate content based on engagement metrics. Likes, shares, clicks, rather than truthfulness or public interest. This shift has contributed to what many scholars refer to as an epistemic crisis in journalism. And the heart of this crisis is the blurring of lines between facts and fiction. AI often prioritizes sensationalism to maximize engagement and amplify misleading or force information at the expense of reliable reporting. This undermines journalism's credibility and erodes public trust, which are both crucial for a healthy democracy.
fragments.summary: Journalism has traditionally been the backbone of democracy, guiding public understanding of complex issues through investigation and ethical reporting.

fragments.text: Every technological shift in history has brought risks and dilemmas, and AI is no exception. What's new is the scale, intensity, and pace. AI is not only the latest, but also the most disruptive one. It demands careful recalibration of our values and practices. As we move forward, the question isn't whether AI will shape journalism, but how we can make sure it is used responsibly. The feature of journalism in these circumstances depends on finding the way to uphold the principles that have long defined the profession. AI is here to stay and will continue to evolve. That's why also media organizations themselves need to be proactive and must prevent AI from undermining journalism's core mission.
fragments.summary: Every technological shift in history has brought risks and dilemmas, and AI is no exception.
